operations.name: Juanita McKamey

expected.name: Juanita McKamey
expected.description: Juanita McKamey was an Industrial Workers of the World activist in the San Diego free speech fight. Police arrested her on February 8, 1912, for participating in the campaign against the street-speaking restriction. She spent the night in the city jail and was released on bail the next morning. She later faced juvenile detention and probation proceedings. Historian Steve Rossignol records her release from those proceedings and dismissal of her case on August 22, 1912. That later detention was separate from her initial overnight imprisonment.

operations.source: Original San Diego police identification card in the collection of Shayne Davidson, reproduced and individually identified by its owner: https://capturedandexposedcom.wordpress.com/2020/12/28/san-diegos-joan-of-arc/ . Original image: https://capturedandexposedcom.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/juanita-mckamey_low_marked.jpg . Full card retained without alterations or removal of its watermark; see CREDITS-batch889.md. No dates inferred from the card examination field.

operations.name: John Michael Donner

expected.name: John Michael Donner
expected.description: Lead-named defendant in United States v. Donner, the federal case against the Beaver 55 for destroying 1-A and delinquent draft files in 44 local boards at the Indianapolis Selective Service headquarters on Oct 31, 1969. Convicted on all four counts (one count later reversed on appeal); originally sentenced to four years, reduced to three. By 1974 he had joined the Divine Light Mission and become its National Executive Director.

operations.source: Contemporary prisoner correspondence appeal in Divine Light Mission publications, Golden Age no. 23: https://prem-rawat-bio.org/dlm_pubs/goldenage/23/festivalfinances.html ; Brotherly Love August 1975: https://www.prem-rawat-bio.org/dlm_pubs/brotherlylove/7508/blove.html . Both individually name John Michael Donner with federal register number. Projected parole after one year is not treated as actual release.
